content.title: 2023-2025 Cadillac Lyriq One-Pedal Driving (OPD) Defect - Class Action Investigation | Sauder Schelkopf
content.text: Sauder Schelkopf is investigating a potential class action lawsuit on behalf of owners and lessees of 2023-2025 Cadillac Lyriq electric vehicles related to claims that the vehicle’s One-Pedal Driving (OPD)/regenerative braking mode and brake-assist system may fail unexpectedly. Owners report that while driving, the Lyriq’s OPD mode or brake-assist feature suddenly becomes unavailable or disengages, often accompanied by warnings such as “One-Pedal Driving Unavailable,” “Brake Assist Off,” or “Auto-Hold Unavailable.” Some drivers say this happens while decelerating behind another vehicle, which they allege significantly increases the risk of a rear-end collision or other crash. Some consumers further allege that when they presented their Lyriq vehicles to Cadillac/GM dealerships for inspection, the dealership’s diagnostics found no permanent fix, or advised that the situation was “normal mode switching,” rather than acknowledging a systemic defect. If you have experienced sudden loss of one-pedal driving/regenerative braking, brake assist disabling, or related warning messages in your 2023-2025 Cadillac Lyriq, please contact the lawyers at Sauder Schelkopf by filling out the form on this page.
